svg.title: What happens when you Forget
svg.desc: Three steps run in one transaction under the write lock: work out the scope and everything derived from it, record the revocation and prune projections, then delete the sealed bytes, sealed text and wrapped keys and write the erasure receipt. At the commit, every read refuses the captures and late writes into the range are refused. After the commit, the store truncates the write-ahead log. If nothing holds the log, the receipt is stamped complete. If a reader holds it, the erasure stays pending and a later writer finishes it.
svg.text: What happens when you Forget
One transaction, under the write lock
BEGIN IMMEDIATE to COMMIT
Lock, then work out the set
The captures the scope names, and everything derived from them, through derived_from.
Record the revocation
The revocation and the revoked set. Every projection is pruned, with a receipt each.
Erase the content
Delete the sealed payloads, the sealed text and the wrapped keys. Deleted cells are zeroed
(secure_delete). Write the erasure receipt, with completed_at empty.
Commit: the Forget has happened
From this moment every read refuses these captures, under every grant, open readers included.
A write stamped in a revoked time range, or derived from a revoked capture, is refused.
After the commit
Truncate the write-ahead log
The log still holds the frames that wrote the content. PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE),
retried for about a second.
Nothing holds the log
The log is truncated. The receipt gets
completed_at. erasedOnDisk is true.
A reader holds the log
The receipt stays pending. The next writer
to open the store finishes it, or the app's
next tick, or the next pcap command.
